note: Status is stated by the PM and checked against the repository: built = implemented, run on real NASA data, with automated tests of the code; partial = core implemented, missing parts stated; designed = specification only. Built does not mean scientifically validated. When a function is built, change its status here; nothing else changes.

items.name: Tamper-evident ledger
items.summary: Append-only, hash-chained, Ed25519-signed record of every ingest, derivation and qualification; anchored in Git and RFC 3161.

items.name: Verification in your browser
items.summary: Every ledger entry and every data file shown on the page re-checked by the visitor's browser, byte-identical to the Python verifier. Raw NASA bytes are not published with the page.

items.name: Evidence Vault
items.summary: Primary files and source tables sealed as tiers 1–2; two keys with separate roles. Write-once storage and the seal event are designed.

items.name: Portable black box
items.summary: The sealed core of a project on a USB stick, verifiable offline anywhere.

items.name: Deviation register
items.summary: Every source conflict and every own error recorded with locators and affected results.

items.name: W3C PROV-O export
items.summary: The ledger exported as standard provenance (JSON-LD): 179 entities, 91 derivation links, 32 revisions, parsed by an RDF library.

items.name: Fire-safety evidence map
items.summary: For seven fire-safety functions: which of NASA's 24 PSI combustion investigations give evidence, under which stated conditions, and between which a finding may be carried. Two AI extractors, every value checked word for word against NASA's record, transfer decided by fixed rules. Record level: no quantitative conditions.

items.name: Transfer assessment engine
items.summary: Deterministic decision on whether a finding can inform another context; refuses with the blocking dimension named. For BASS-II run pairs the gate states are computed from measured data; for the PMMA-100 literature case they are declared from the source audit and labelled so.

items.name: Canonical evidence graph
items.summary: Sources, experiments, samples, measurements, claims and assessments as typed nodes; unresolved links are never drawn as joins. One case, two layers: the published B3 records, and the seven runs GFL measured with their rates, sealed predictions and computed transfer assessments, generated from the sealed results. Other cases are not built.

items.name: Comparable-run ranking
items.summary: Every row of NASA's BASS-II experimental table ranked against B6, condition by condition; unknown counts against. Ranks what the table records, not physical equivalence.

items.name: Physics gates computed from data
items.summary: Transfer gates computed from measured and recorded values (ruleset v0.2): run identity, observable, material and thickness, atmosphere and calibrated flow, regime, boundary conditions. Regime boundaries are order-of-magnitude.

items.name: Held-out transferability
items.summary: Four predictions sealed before the runs were acquired: 1 supported, 1 not supported, 2 not testable. Across oxygen, two 17 % runs are measured (B19, B20); the third (B16) is too dim for the frozen rule (ISS-029), so the cross-oxygen test is not complete.

items.name: Literature relevance and comparability
items.summary: Relevance built with NASA's INDUS encoder, twice: over the project's paper library for each open question, and over NASA's records of the 24 PSI combustion investigations for seven fire-safety questions. Indexing published papers by their conditions, for comparability, is designed.

items.name: Evidence-backed synthesis
items.summary: AI-written summaries of findings in which every sentence cites records, checked automatically (citations exist, numbers appear in the cited records). General synthesis across sources is designed.

items.name: Validated predictive models
items.summary: Built: two laws with a stated domain (inverse thickness for thin fuel, flow independence in the thermal regime), a domain check that refuses outside it, sealing before the data are opened, and scoring that carries the reference uncertainty. Tested on held-out runs: 1 supported, 1 not supported, 2 not testable. Not built: a fitted model across flow and oxygen; nothing here is called validated.

items.name: NASA data intelligence
items.summary: PSI-25 manifest of 695 files with sizes; 31 files (7.1 GiB) acquired with SHA-256 and re-downloaded identically; filename–table joins flagged, never corrected.

items.name: Flame-front measurement
items.summary: Frozen window rule (R-W4) as a platform module; four runs measured, identity confirmed against NASA proof sheets; B6 re-run byte-identical. Built does not mean validated: the luminous edge is not the pyrolysis front.

items.name: Uncertainty in three layers
items.summary: Statistical, analyst-choice and physical-unknown layers kept apart; the luminous-edge offset and the flow at the sample have no bound and stay outside the interval.

items.name: Data-quality anomaly detection
items.summary: Records, frames and flow overlay checked with declared thresholds; finds every detectable anomaly planted in the synthetic test and flags 24 items in NASA's table (for example final O2 1.6 % in B2, and final O2 near 40 % in two tests that started at 20 %).

items.name: CRAM-1 thin-fuel theory
items.summary: de Ris, Delichatsios and EST thin-fuel rates with sourced PMMA properties; measured / lowest theory falls from 1.04 (100 µm) to 0.79 (400 µm). Never uses the fitted F = 4.76.

items.name: CRAM-2 combustion regime
items.summary: Damköhler and radiation numbers from the calibrated flow: thermal at air display 3 and above, transitional at 1–2, radiative side at 0. Order-of-magnitude boundaries; says when chemistry matters, does not model it.

items.name: Oxygen sensitivity
items.summary: From measured runs only: how the spread rate of the 100 µm film changes between 21 % and 17 % oxygen, with the intervals of both runs carried into the ratio and the local exponent. No flame temperature is assumed; the result is stated as a constraint on the thin-fuel formula. Exploratory, two oxygen levels.

items.name: CRAM-3 nonlinear dynamics
items.summary: Flame-area and front oscillation tested against surrogate data.

items.name: Flow calibration
items.summary: Air display to opposing-flow speed from NASA's fan calibration (U = 1.0066 × display, duct centreline); the speed at the sample surface stays unknown.

items.name: Other NASA combustion families
items.summary: BASS-II acquired and measured. The other families in NASA's PSI repository (Saffire, SAME, FLEX, ACME, SLICE and others) are mapped at record level in the evidence map and kept separate, not pooled; none of them is measured by GFL.

items.name: Reproducible analysis runs
items.summary: One command rebuilds the release results in an empty copy and compares each with its sealed fingerprint: 30 of 30 identical from NASA's raw stills (RES-051). The rebuild from derived files runs with the tests on every change; the one from raw files needs the NASA download.

items.name: Physical model and parameter registry
items.summary: Every equation and property the theory and regime modules use, in one table: value, unit, source, and which model uses it, found by changing the value and seeing which outputs move. Five of fifteen values are approximate and marked so. Literature values, not the BASS-II PMMA lot.

items.name: Experiment memory
items.summary: Every result, decision, issue and idea with its history, citations and sealed files; failures kept as records.

items.name: Analysis records
items.summary: One report per relevant analysis: question, method, deviations, results, limits, reproduction. One record exists so far (AR-001).

items.name: Blind independent analyses (AAL)
items.summary: AI analysts work without seeing GFL results; their code is re-executed by GFL. Two blind tests and one independent evaluation done, with defects and scores recorded (RES-019, RES-034, RES-053). Run by hand through AAL and scripts, not as an automated pipeline.

items.name: AI findings, ranked by verification
items.summary: Claims made by seven AI models in blind, red-team and audit roles, ranked by what GFL's re-execution and data checks showed: upheld, partly upheld, not upheld, fabricated.

items.name: AI access over MCP
items.summary: Read-only MCP server: any AI client can query the memory, a record, the ledger check, the run ranking, the transfer engine and the AI findings; answers name their sources. Checked with a client GFL did not write, the official MCP SDK: handshake, six tools listed as read-only, six tools answered. Blind mode and an in-page assistant are designed.

items.name: Enriched-oxygen atmospheres
items.summary: Which existing results may inform an exploration cabin with more oxygen at lower pressure, with the gap to measured conditions shown and never extrapolated across.

items.name: Partial gravity: Moon and Mars
items.summary: Gravity as a continuous condition through an effective opposed flow, so microgravity and Earth results can be placed on one axis for 0.17 g and 0.38 g.

items.name: Earth applications
items.summary: What low-flow flight evidence may inform confined, poorly ventilated fires on Earth; and the same ledger and evidence-map method on any other experimental archive.

items.name: Multiphysics simulation
items.summary: Coupled gas–solid simulation to test what measurements cannot isolate; outputs are derived evidence, never measurements.

items.name: Fire-scenario analysis
items.summary: For a cabin scenario: which experiments give relevant evidence, what transfers, what does not. The record-level evidence map is the first step and is built; scenario input and run-level conditions are not.

items.name: Model predictive control
items.summary: What a real MPC would need: a validated dynamic model, horizon, objective, constraints and solver. Not part of the product.

items.name: ECLSS decision support
items.summary: Evidence views for environmental-control engineers, with stated limits; never an automatic action.

items.name: Sensor integration
items.summary: New measurement streams sealed with instrument records and explicit clock offsets.

items.name: Dynamic dependency analysis
items.summary: Correlation, mutual information and transfer entropy between burn time series, tested against surrogates.

items.name: State estimation
items.summary: Kalman-type filtering of front position and speed; needs a second, non-luminous front observation.
